tasks.title: Secure unauthenticated PUT /api/profile/[id]/update
tasks.description:

Nothing in src/ or e2e/ fetches this endpoint, and all three helpers (isEmailInUse, validateCompanyAccess, updateUserProfile) are setTimeout/Math.random stubs with no Prisma access. It is unfinished scaffolding, not a live feature. Recommended fix: delete src/app/api/profile/[id]/update/route.ts outright rather than gate it — deleting removes the unauthenticated PUT with zero behavior change, and whoever builds the real endpoint later starts with withAuth from day one.

tasks.title: REA-DRT-07 — Bridge SSR cookie to browser supabase-js session (Realtime never initializes)
tasks.description:
DONE — shipped in PR #409 (merged 2026-05-22), live on apex via #412. Remaining: confirm Sentry READY-SET-NEXTJS-1S goes silent with an authenticated apex check.

Root cause (investigated 2026-05-19): server-side cookie defaults force httpOnly: true on every cookie they write — including the sb-<ref>-auth-token chunks. src/utils/supabase/server.ts:10-16 and src/utils/supabase/middleware.ts:6-12 both define { httpOnly: true, ...options } defaults, and @supabase/ssr doesn't override httpOnly, so the auth cookies land HttpOnly. The browser supabase-js client (src/utils/supabase/client.ts:19-28) reads cookies via document.cookie, which by spec cannot see HttpOnly cookies — so getSession() returns null, Realtime channels never authenticate, and TokenRefreshService throws REFRESH_FAILED (the symptom #404 patched as graceful failure). Regression introduced in commit f49f6ec5 (2026-01-07 mobile-Safari ITP fix); the sameSite: 'lax' + request+response sync changes in that commit were correct, only httpOnly: true was wrong.

Fix: drop httpOnly: true from getDefaultCookieOptions (server.ts) and getCookieOptions (middleware.ts); auth cookies must be JS-readable for the @supabase/ssr SSR↔browser bridge. ~2-line change in 2 files. Add a browser getSession() smoke test in src/lib/auth/__tests__/token-refresh-and-session.test.ts that fails if auth cookies are written HttpOnly.

Tradeoff: XSS-exfiltrable auth tokens in principle; mitigated by existing CSP + dompurify + Supabase's short-lived JWT + refresh-token rotation. Keep #404 patch in place — graceful sign-in redirect on legitimate session expiry is still correct behavior.

Out of scope: Realtime reconnect handler (see docs/architecture/REMEDIATION_PLAN.md). See docs/JOURNAL.md 2026-05-19 for full trace.

tasks.title: REA-367 — Realtime channel.off() cleanup throws (channel closes ~1ms after subscribe)
tasks.description:
RealtimeChannelManager.off() (src/lib/realtime/channels.ts:168-173) calls this.channel.off('broadcast', { event }, listener), but the Supabase RealtimeChannel has no runtime .off() — that's a Phoenix Channels method present only via a .d.ts type augmentation. So cleanup throws TypeError: this.channel.off is not a function; the catch only swallows 'closed' / 'not found' / 'already removed' messages, so it logs a WARN and the channel tears down — the admin driver-locations channel reaches subscribed then closes ~1ms later.

Fix: drop the per-event off() path and tear down via client.removeChannel(channel) / channel.unsubscribe() (supabase-js v2 has no per-callback removal).

Confirmed live during REA-DRT-07 verification on 2026-05-20 (channel subscribed → cleanup TypeError → closed). Blocks DRT-06+. Promoted from QA fail REA-DRT-05 (sub-step DT5-01, Critical).

DONE (PR #410, merged 2026-05-22, live via #412): fixed in PR #410 (stable broadcast dispatcher; removed the phantom channel.off() + its .d.ts augmentation; 38 tests). The TypeError + cleanup WARN are verified gone. The remaining subscribe→close (StrictMode) is split to rea-367b-realtime-strictmode-resubscribe.

tasks.title: Realtime channel closes after subscribe under React StrictMode (no re-subscribe)
tasks.description:
Split from REA-367. After the channel.off fix (PR #410), the admin driver-locations channel still reaches subscribed then closes ~1ms later in dev and does not re-subscribe.

Root cause is a React StrictMode double-invoke race in useAdminRealtimeTracking (src/hooks/tracking/useAdminRealtimeTracking.ts:512-534): mount 1's deferred .then cleanup (lines 518-523) calls removeChannel('driver-locations') on the channel mount 2 established (the RealtimeClient dedups by channel name), tearing it down with no re-subscribe. StrictMode double-invoke is dev-only, so production single-mount is unaffected — but it blocks dev/QA (DRT-06+).

Fix direction: ref-count or guard the shared channel so a stale mount's cleanup can't remove a channel a live mount owns (or key channels per-subscriber). Verify on development.readysetllc.com (prod build, no StrictMode double-invoke) after #410 merges. Found during #410 verification on 2026-05-20.

Re-verified 2026-08-03: still broken — no generation/instance guard; isMountedRef is a one-way latch (never reset on remount), and the deferred .then cleanups still unsubscribe channelRef.current instead of the captured local channel.

2026-09-02 Android walk — RESULT: FAIL (hard numbers). Aziel, real device, CDMX Chapultepec, shift 52bf8a9c 83.4 min, 230 GPS points, 2.33 km, avg accuracy 2.6 m (accuracy was never the problem). Trail gap analysis vs the ~30 s pass bar: 22 gaps >30 s, 13 >60 s, 7 >120 s, worst 564 s (9.4 min).
The split is the finding — cut at the pickup (23:59:03Z, when the phone was backgrounded):
• Screen on (176 intervals): avg 8.3 s, median 7.9 s, max 45.9 s, 1 gap >30 s.
• Backgrounded (53 intervals): avg 66.6 s, median 19.7 s, max 564.5 s, 21 gaps >30 s.
8× degradation the moment the app stops being foreground. Foreground tracking is healthy; background tracking is not — this is the Android-side reproduction of the bug, not a permissions or accuracy artifact.

tasks.description:

Phase 2 of the background-GPS plan — must be fixed before real-driver rollout of the native app. Related: persistent-gps-background.

Update 2026-08-17 — symptom class fixed, verified on-device. The bounce turned out to be redirect-class, not URL-specific: any server-side redirect() on the entry URL blanked the WebView and bounced to Safari (reinstall-over preserves WKWebsiteDataStore cookies, so even /sign-in 307'd when authed). Fix = the /native-launch zero-redirect entry page (web PR #514, merged 2026-08-13) + wrapper entry flip (a1893d43). Verified 2026-08-13 on the iPhone 16 Pro Max in the cookie-carrying state. The Aug 12 drives also moved driver API calls to Bearer-token transport (PR #513), sidestepping the stale-cookie 401 split for POD/end-shift. Keep open only to watch for residual cookie-vs-token drift during the remaining locked-screen walk; if none surfaces, close.

tasks.title: iOS wrapper: log out bounces to Safari and the user cannot actually log out
tasks.description:
Reported 2026-09-03 (Emmanuel, iOS wrapper). Tapping log out opens Safari instead of staying in the app, and the log out never completes — the user stays signed in.

Cause: src/app/(site)/(users)/driver/page.tsx:99 ends the handler with window.location.href = "/sign-in". This is the same trap /native-launch was created to avoid: capacitor.config.ts documents that /sign-in issues a redirect when a session is still present, and any 307 on a WKWebView navigation fails the provisional load and bounces the user out to Safari. The "cannot log out" half is consistent with the known WebView cookie/session divergence (native-shell-session-divergence): supabase.auth.signOut() clears the client session while the server-side cookie survives, so /sign-in still redirects as authenticated.

Fix direction: send log out to /native-launch (the only route that answers 200 in every auth state) rather than /sign-in, and make sign-out clear the server cookie — not just the client session — so the redirect decision agrees with the client. Sibling of wrapper-post-login-safari-bounce: same root cause on the way out instead of the way in.

Update 2026-10-05: fix shipped in #606 (server sign-out route + performSignOut() → /native-launch, live in 2.9.3). Remaining: confirm log out on a device inside the iOS wrapper.

tasks.title: Queued GPS point arrives hours later, after its shift closed
tasks.description:
Found in the 10-16 readiness re-run. Fernando's iPhone recorded a point at 10-15 21:04Z (shift ddf14bac) that reached the server at 10-16 00:04Z, 3 h later, during his next shift (55df7546). Almost certainly the service-worker offline queue (public/service-worker.js) replaying on the next page load.

What is fine: /api/tracking/locations keeps the device time (resolveRecordedAt accepts up to 24 h back) and mileage (src/services/tracking/mileage.ts) selects by recorded_at, so the point is filed under the right shift.

What is not: (1) the first shift's miles were computed at End shift, before the point arrived, so stored mileage misses late points; (2) the realtime broadcast fires on insert, so the live admin map may jump to a 3-hour-old position mid-shift (verify). Fix: skip the live broadcast / marker update when recorded_at is older than the driver's latest point; recompute a closed shift's mileage when a late point lands inside it (or drop queued points older than the shift end). Low severity: 1 point in the 60-day data.
